A feedback survey of what worked and what to change, analysed as text: frequent words and phrases, words in context, sentiment and topics. surveyframe gives you the questionnaire, the analysis plan and the report.

## Preview the questionnaire

This is the questionnaire as respondents see it. It is a preview, so answers go nowhere. [Open it in a new tab](../../templates/open_text/preview.html).

```{=html}
<iframe src="../../templates/open_text/preview.html" title="Preview of the Open-ended feedback survey questionnaire" style="width:100%;height:560px;border:1px solid #d9e2ec;border-radius:6px"></iframe>
```

## The analysis plan, ready to preregister

Before any data is collected, surveyframe writes the pre-analysis plan: the study, the questionnaire, each research question with its hypotheses, method and decision rule, and what a preregistration still asks for. [Read the plan](../../templates/open_text/plan.html), or [download the instrument (.sframe)](../../templates/open_text/open_text.sframe) and open it in SurveyStudio.

Methods it declares: Word frequencies, Phrase frequencies, Words in context, Word co-occurrence, Word co-occurrence network, Sentiment analysis, Document-feature matrix, Topic model (LDA), Structural topic model.

## Start in 2 steps (no coding)

1. Install surveyframe in R: `install.packages("surveyframe")`
2. In RStudio, open the Addins menu, choose **surveyframe: Try a demo**, and pick `open_text`. The study opens in SurveyStudio.

## Questions

### What can surveyframe do with open answers?

Word and phrase frequencies, keywords in context, co-occurrence, sentiment, a document-feature matrix and topic models.

### Can I compare groups?

Yes. The plan can compare what in-person and online respondents write.

### Does it replace reading the answers?

No. It shows where to look, and the report keeps the quotes that represent each topic.

## For R users

```{=html}
<details><summary>Open this study in R</summary>
```

```r
d <- sframe_demo("open_text")
render_report(d$instrument)                 # the pre-analysis plan
results <- run_analysis_plan(d$responses, d$instrument)
```
